newsitem.title: USA: Plenty of seats available for Kerry fundraiser.
newsitem.headline: Plenty of seats available for Kerry fundraiser.

text.p: President Clinton should not feel bad -- even the Boston Bruins and the Celtics are having a hard time selling tickets and attracting fans these days.

The president is the headliner at this Saturday's fundraiser concert for Democratic Sen. John Kerry at the Fleet Center in Boston. As of Tuesday, there were still plenty of tickets available in all categories, from the $25 seats up by the arena's rafters to the $1,000 chairs at ground level.
A $25,000 contribution includes a post-concert dinner with Clinton.

Kerry is not just banking on Clinton's drawing power, or his saxaphone. The back-to-the '60s concert lineup includes top names like Peter, Paul and Mary, Carly Simon, ex-Eagle Don Henley and Crosby, Stills and Nash.
The Fleet Center, which is home to the Bruins hockey team and the Celtics basketball team, can hold up to 19,580 seats for a concert.

But Kerry campaign spokesman Dwight Robson said Secret Service requirements would severely limit seating capacity for the event. Robson said the campaign would not be releasing the total number of seats sold, nor the number left.
"There are seats available in all categories," Robson said. "But we're not going to get into a daily horserace here."
Tickets were available through TicketMaster, the Fleet Center box office and Kerry's campaign offices.
Boston concert promoter Don Law is marketing the concert, advertising in local newspapers, while a series of television ads is scheduled this week promoting the event.
A spokesman for the Bruins confirmed a report that ticket sales for the 1996-97 season for both his team and the Celtics were lagging.
